title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Samira Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This playbook defines the standardized process for enterprise customer onboarding, system integration, escalation handling, known-issues tracking and workarounds, and health-check/QBR preparation for Redwood Inference. It provides checklists, step-by-step procedures, ownership, SLAs, and example artifacts to ensure consistent, low-friction customer experience and fast operational response.

Scope
-----
Applies to: customer-success, solutions engineering, support, eng-infra, eng-platform, and SRE teams for customers that are using Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.

Key objectives:
- Deliver repeatable, low-risk onboarding that reaches production readiness within agreed timelines.
- Provide clear escalation channels and response SLAs based on severity.
- Document integration best-practices and required configuration for production traffic.
- Maintain a concise known-issues inventory with actionable workarounds.
- Produce repeatable QBR artifacts and health checks to measure success and retention risk.

Roles & ownership
------------------
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall customer relationship, QBR owner, primary business contact.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical lead for integration, runbooks, pre-go-live validation (API keys, routing, throughput).
- Support Engineer (Tier 1/2): triage, initial troubleshooting, logging, and replication steps.
- Platform/SRE Oncall: investigates production incidents and infrastructure issues.
- Product Owner: approves product-related change requests and feature rollouts.

Onboarding lifecycle (high level)
--------------------------------
1. Discovery (Week 0): document use-cases, success metrics, data residency & compliance requirements, and expected QPS/throughput.
2. Architecture & Security Review (Week 0-1): capture networking (VPC, firewall), KMS/HSM needs, and confirm private/dedicated requirements.
3. Integration & PoC (Week 1-3): hook up API keys, implement client SDK calls, run sample workloads, and capture perf baseline.
4. Validation & Hardening (Week 3-4): run load tests, enable caching/batching recommendations, validate SLOs and fallback policies.
5. Go-Live & Stabilization (Week 4-6): enable production routing, monitor for errors, complete runbook handoff.
6. QBR & Handover (Month 1+): present initial health, SLA attainment, and next-phase roadmap.

Onboarding checklist (detailed)
------------------------------
Pre-engagement:
- Signed contract and support tier confirmed.
- CSM assigned and kickoff scheduled.
- Security questionnaire completed.

Kickoff meeting agenda:
- Introductions & roles
- Scope, success metrics, timelines
- High-level architecture and data flow
- Compliance and data residency constraints
- Integration milestones and sign-off criteria

Integration tasks (owner: SE)
- Provision API keys and scopes (expires/rotation policy)
- Confirm endpoint selection: hosted (api.redwood.com), dedicated hostname, or private control plane URL.
- Provide client SDK quickstart snippet and sample curl.

Sample curl (integration smoke test):
``
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

Required configuration table (copy into customer runbook)
| Item | Typical value / requirement | Owner | Notes |
|------|----------------------------|-------|-------|
| API Host | api.redwood.com or customer-specific host | SE | Use region-specific host for latency-sensitive customers |
| Rate limit | 1,200 requests/min (customizable) | SE/CSM | Adjust per contract; set quotas in console |
| Tokenization | UTF-8; tokens per request limit 64k seq for large-context models | SE | Monitor token budgeting for cost |
| Authentication | API key + optional mTLS for Private | Security | For Private deployments use customer KMS |
| Logging & Audit | Request/response IDS, sampling 1% | Customer-success/Support | Ensure redaction of PII before sharing logs |

Validation & performance gates
- Perf baseline: capture median and p95 latency for target model(s) at expected QPS.
- Error rate: <0.5% 5xx during PoC period.
- Cost estimate: projected monthly token spend validated by CSM.
- Security: penetration test and SOC2 checklist items completed for Private deployments.

Go-live checklist (owner: CSM + SE + Support)
1. All integration tests passed for production endpoints.
2. Rate limits and quotas applied correctly.
3. Alerting and dashboards configured.
4. Rollout policy set (canary % and automatic fallback).
5. Runbooks and escalation matrix delivered to customer.
6. Post-go-live monitoring window agreed (typical 72 hours).

Support process & ticket workflow
--------------------------------
1. Customer files ticket via support portal or designated channel.
2. Tier 1 Support acknowledges within SLA (see SLAs below) and attempts replication.
3. If unresolved after 60 minutes (for sev-1) or 4 hours (sev-2), escalate to Tier 2/SE.
4. If platform issue suspected, page Platform/SRE oncall and attach diagnostics.
5. For security incidents, follow security incident playbook and notify Security team immediately.

Support SLAs (internal target)
- Severity 1 (System down / production outage): initial response 15 minutes; update cadence 30 minutes until mitigation.
- Severity 2 (Partial outage / major feature broken): initial response 1 hour; updates every 2 hours.
- Severity 3 (Degradation / non-urgent bugs): initial response 4 business hours; weekly updates.
- Severity 4 (General questions / feature requests): initial response 1 business day.

Escalation playbook
-------------------
Severity definitions and actions:
- Sev-1 (P1): Customer-facing production outage; immediate page to SRE + CSM; continuous updates until resolved.
  * Pager: Platform oncall via PagerDuty (PD) -> primary oncall.
  * Escalation steps: support -> SE -> SRE oncall -> Eng manager -> Product owner.

- Sev-2 (P2): Significant impact, limited functionality. Support + SE triage; SRE involvement if infrastructure. Updates every 2 hours.

Triage checklist (first 30 minutes):
1. Collect customer request id, region, model, timestamp, and sample payload.
2. Capture logs (request id, router trace, model backend id) and relevant metrics (p95 latency, 5xx rate).
3. Determine scope (single user, tenant, region-wide).
4. Confirm whether change/failure is customer config, model behavior, or infra.
5. Apply mitigation (traffic-shift, fallback model, restart worker pool) as appropriate.

Escalation matrix (contact order):
1. Tier 1 Support: support-team@redwood.com (Slack #support)
2. Solutions Engineer (assigned): se-<customer>@redwood.com
3. Platform/SRE oncall: paged via PagerDuty (primary SRE)
4. Engineering Manager: eng-manager@redwood.com
5. Product Owner: product-owner@redwood.com

Known issues & workarounds (top items)
------------------------------------
1. Intermittent 504 at peak QPS from upstream load balancer
- Symptom: p95 latency spikes with 504s reported.
- Workaround: temporarily reduce client concurrency and enable request-level retries with exponential backoff; route to a model variant with lower memory footprint.

2. Unexpectedly high token charge from long user messages
- Symptom: monthly bill spike due to user-provided long documents.
- Workaround: enforce client-side truncation policy, implement token-count middleware, or use summarization preprocessor.

3. KV cache miss storm after model restart
- Symptom: sudden latency increase after pool recycle.
- Workaround: stagger restarts, enable warm-up requests, or use sticky routing to keep active caches.

4. Webhook delivery failures (403/401) for Private deployments
- Symptom: customer reports webhook auth failure after upgrade.
- Workaround: confirm webhook signing key rotation, verify network egress rules and TLS trust stores.

5. Quantization artifacting (inference quality drop for quantized variant)
- Symptom: regression in metrics for specific prompts.
- Workaround: fallback to higher-precision variant for affected routes and open a model regression ticket with Applied ML.

Known-issues table (copyable)
| ID | Symptom | Likely cause | Temporary mitigation | Owner |
|----|---------|--------------|---------------------|-------|
| KI-128 | 504 spikes at peak | Upstream LB timeout | Reduce concurrency, retry | Platform |
| KI-215 | Cost overrun | Long inputs | Tokenize/truncate | CSM/SE |
| KI-304 | Cache coldstart | Worker recycle | Warm-up traffic | SRE |

Diagnostics & required artifacts for escalation
- Minimum reproducible request and timestamp (server time).
- Request IDs and router trace (X-Req-ID).
- SDK logs at debug level (with PII redacted).
- Snapshot of relevant dashboards (error rate, latency percentiles, model backend health).

Health checks & QBR materials
----------------------------
Standard health dashboard tiles (recommended):
- Total requests per minute (by route/model).
- Token consumption (daily/30-day).
- Error rate (5xx and 4xx) with filter by route.
- Latency p50/p95/p99 by model.
- Cost per 1,000 tokens and month-to-date spend.
- Cache hit ratio and batching efficiency.

Health-check weekly checklist (owner: CSM + SE)
- Verify alerts are green and no recent Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents.
- Confirm API key rotation schedule is on-track.
- Review top 10 erroring routes and assign action owners.
- Observe cost vs projection and flag anomalies.

QBR template (30-60 minute meeting)
1. Executive summary (uptime, key wins, major incidents).
2. Metrics review (traffic, latency, error rate, cost).
3. Project roadmap and upcoming rollouts.
4. Action items and owners (from 30d retros).
5. Risk review and recommendations (scaling, batching, model variants).

Suggested QBR slides (copy into deck):
- Title: Customer QBR - Redwood Inference
- Slide 1: Executive summary (1 slide)
- Slide 2: Traffic & performance (graphs)
- Slide 3: Cost analysis & optimization opportunities
- Slide 4: Reliability & incidents (timeline + RCA links)
- Slide 5: Roadmap & requests
- Slide 6: Action items and SLA status

Postmortem & RCA expectations
-----------------------------
- For Sev-1 incidents impacting SLAs, publish a postmortem within 72 hours with follow-up actions and owners.
- RCA must include timeline, root cause, immediate mitigation, long-term fix, and verification plan.

Automations & runbook links
--------------------------
- Enable automated alerting to Slack channels used by the CSM and oncall.
- Use pre-built runbooks for common mitigations (traffic-shift, fallback to model-variant, worker pool recycle).
- Reference runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks and /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/coldstart-mitigation.

Templates & artifacts included
----------------------------
- Onboarding runbook template (copyable)
- Integration acceptance test checklist
- Escalation email and Slack templates
- Known-issues CSV template
- QBR slide deck template

Operational metrics to track (recommended KPIs)
- Time to first production request (days)
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) per severity
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for Sev-1/2
- Post-onboarding retention rate at 90 days

Appendix: Common CLI & debug commands
- Capture router trace: `REDWOOD_TRACE=1 curl ...` (include X-Req-ID)
- Download recent logs: `redwoodctl logs --tenant <tenant-id> --since 30m`
- Re-route traffic to fallback: `redwoodctl route set --route <route> --model <model-variant> --weight 0.0`

Change history
--------------
- 2025-11-15: Created by Samira Patel (initial published playbook).
- 2026-03-04: Major update - clarified SLAs, added known-issues table, and QBR template.

Contact & escalation directory
-----------------------------
- Global Support: support@redwood.com (24x7 for Sev-1s)
- Partner SEs: se-partners@redwood.com
- PagerDuty: platform-sre-oncall (primary)
- Customer Success leadership: csm-leads@redwood.com

This playbook should be copied into each customer-specific runbook and customized for contract-specific SLAs, quotas, and architecture. For changes to this playbook, submit PR to the Customer Success handbook and notify reviewers listed above.
